newsitem.title: USA: San Onofre Calif. nuke unit outage may be extended.
newsitem.headline: San Onofre Calif. nuke unit outage may be extended.

text.p: The current refueling outage of the 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant near San Clemente, Calif., could be extended by 10 or 15 days, a spokesman for the plant said Tuesday.
The unit has been down for refueling and maintenance since November 30 and was scheduled to restart February 8, said spokesman Ray Golden.
But routine inspection of the unit's steam generator tubes revealed the need for some plugging, which may result in the delay, he added.
A final estimate for the outage schedule will be made next week, Golden said.
San Onofre's other operating unit, the 1,080 MW unit 3, was said to be running at full power.
Unit 3's next refueling outage is scheduled for 65 days starting April 5.
The units are operated and majority-owned by Edison International's Southern California Edison Co.
San Diego Gas and Electric Co, a subsidiary of Enova Corp, owns 20 pct of the plant, while the cities of Anaheim and Riverside own the remaining five percent.
